tool_args.rationale: Fresh confirmation refuted the prior gradient-coupled saturation model, but did not show chaotic behavior. The expanded notes and acquired variation support the bridge-to-inland-hub siphon law: a saturating u_now pool, sink-gradient inhibition, and an open square-root branch. Refit this law numerically on all paid rows rather than spending further on fixed-horizon trajectory data.

considered_alternatives.option: extra_fine_trajectory_batch for a coupled memory ODE
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: The existing batch already supplies 10 rows, but u_past, x_now, H and mem_conv remain fixed; trajectory data cannot identify a temporal ODE. The observed variation is strongly associated with s_grad and u_now, matching the static siphon source family.
Open-branch discrimination has already been acquired and yields diverse gradients. The observed gradients do not reach the stated avalanche threshold, so a high-sgrad probe is not indicated.

considered_alternatives.option: Gradient-independent Beverton-Holt or other snapshot saturation
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: The two open-branch contrasts and fine-batch rows show substantial gradient dependence, contradicting the gradient-ignoring snapshot law.

It is a plausible competing static mechanism, but the source notes identify the bridge as mapping onto the C inland-hub siphon, and the saturating factor with gradient inhibition and open square-root branch is the simpler supported family.
